We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes. For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work. As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another. At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today. ***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role. A day in the life: You’ll join novaX, Power Digital’s innovation team, which builds internal and external products that help our teams and clients make decisions and get work done, such as Signal, Omega and Iris. You’ll sit in the AI/ML squad, which focuses on statistical modeling. This is a full-stack data role: you build the data systems our products run on, build predictive models on top of them, like scores that show which clients are ready to grow, and put both in front of the people who use them. One day you might trace why a number doesn’t match its source, fix the pipeline and add a test so it can’t drift again. The next you might sit with the people who use a model, learn how they make the decision, and ship a better version where they work. AI is how we build: you’ll use AI coding tools for most of what you ship, so you can take an idea from raw data to a production feature on your own. As an innovation team we move fast: we try ideas, keep what works, drop what doesn’t, and priorities can shift quickly. We’re looking for someone hungry to learn and grow with us along the way. Key Responsibilities: Design, build and own the data systems our products and models run on: pipelines, services and APIs that bring together our warehouse, app databases, spreadsheets and third-party APIs. Build predictive models and take them all the way to production: frame the question with users, build features, test against a baseline, ship the results where people work and keep them healthy. Build with AI every day: use AI coding tools to move faster across the whole stack, and review and test what they produce before it reaches production. Hold what you build to production standards (tests, code review, CI/CD, monitoring and alerts) so bad or late data is caught before a user sees it, and fix the root cause. Turn vague asks into a clear problem, ship a first version fast and improve it from feedback. Share what works (patterns, prompts, tools) so the whole team builds faster. Work with sensitive data, including finance and people data, under strict access rules. Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize business processes Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department Design, build and own the data systems our products and models run on: dbt models, pipelines, services and APIs that bring together our warehouse, app databases, spreadsheets and third-party APIs. Other applicable or related duties as assigned. Role Requirements: You have 5+ years in data engineering, data science or software roles, with hands-on work that ran in production. You’re full-stack across data: you’ve built pipelines or data services, built predictive models, and connected them to something people use. You don’t need to be the deepest expert in each, but you’re comfortable in all of them. You build with AI every day (Claude Code, Cursor or similar) and can show how it changed what you ship. You review, test and own what it writes. You’ve built and experimented with predictive models, and you’re comfortable with work that needs modeling: framing the problem, building features and evaluating against a baseline. You understand statistics well enough to set up a fair test, spot leakage and tell a real effect from noise. You write strong SQL and Python, and you know good engineering basics: version control, testing and code review. You can walk us through one thing you built end to end: the problem, the data, what you shipped, who used it, what failed along the way, and which parts AI wrote. You start from the decision the user is trying to make, not from the data, and you ask until you understand it. You’re a problem solver who learns fast and fails fast: you’d rather ship something small this week and learn from it than plan for a month, and you keep picking up new tools and methods. You write clearly in English and work well async. Nice to have: Snowflake (our warehouse); cloud deployment and orchestration (for example AWS); some Terraform or other infrastructure as code; marketing or client analytics such as churn or expansion; LLM apps or agents. You have hands-on dbt experience in production: you've built and maintained models, tests, documentation and incremental builds. Most of our transformation work runs on dbt. This is a remote role open to candidates in [the US or Latin America], at [senior, IC4–IC5]. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Reliability: the systems you own meet their agreed freshness and uptime targets, most issues are caught by your checks before a user reports them, and any that slip are resolved within a week. Models in production: every model you ship is monitored, and a change ships only when it beats the current version on held-out data. Adoption: everything you ship has a named user and a usage target agreed with your manager, and at the monthly review you’ve hit it or can explain why. Engineering bar: what you build is tested, documented and reviewable, and a teammate can run it without you. Most Important Things (MITs) In your first 30 days, ship a fix to a production data flow or model. By 90 days, be the go-to owner for one product’s data layer: you review its changes and resolve its issues without escalation. Put one model change into production with a measured before/after. By 6 months, own the production path for a model end to end (data, deployment, monitoring) and have improved how the team builds and ships, with a pattern, test or tool others use.
